title: Opening exhortation and first sayings on virtue, passion, and knowledge
english: To the monks who live in monasteries or in communities.
Heirs of God, listen to the words of God. Co-heirs of Christ, receive the sayings of Christ, so that you may give them to the hearts of your children and teach them the words of the wise.
A good father instructs his sons, but a wicked father will destroy them.
Faith is the beginning of love, and the end of love is knowledge of God.
The fear of the Lord will preserve the soul, and good self-control will strengthen it.
A man's endurance gives birth to hope, and good hope will glorify him.
The one who enslaves his flesh will be free from passions, but the one who indulges it will suffer pain because of it.
A spirit of fornication dwells in the bodies of the self-indulgent, but a spirit of self-control dwells in the souls of the self-controlled.
Withdrawal in love purifies the heart, but withdrawal with hatred throws it into confusion.
Better to be one in a thousand with love than alone with hatred in hidden caves.
The one who stores up resentment in his soul is like someone hiding fire in straw.
Do not give your body too much food, and you will not see evil fantasies in your sleep. For just as a flame consumes a forest, so hunger extinguishes shameful fantasies.
A wrathful man will be terrified, but the gentle man will be without fear.
A strong wind drives away clouds, and resentment drives the mind away from knowledge.
The one who prays for his enemies will be without resentment, and the one who guards his tongue will not grieve his neighbor.

If your brother provokes you, bring him into your house, and do not hesitate to go to him, but eat your morsel with him. For by doing this you will rescue your soul, and there will be no stumbling block for you in the time of prayer.
Just as love rejoices in poverty, so hatred delights in wealth.
A rich man will not attain knowledge, and a camel will not enter the eye of a needle, but nothing will be impossible with the Lord (Matthew 19:24, 26; Mark 10:25, 27).
The one who loves silver will not see knowledge, and the one who hoards it will be darkened.
The Lord will dwell in the tents of the humble, but curses will multiply in the houses of the proud (Proverbs 3:33).
The one who transgresses God's law dishonors God, but the one who keeps it glorifies the one who made it.

If you are zealous for Christ, you will be blessed, and your soul will share his death, and it will not draw evil from its flesh, but your departure will be like the departure of a star, and your resurrection will shine like the sun.
Woe to the lawless man on the day of death, and the unjust man will perish in an evil time. For just as a raven flies away from its nest, so an unclean soul departs from its own body.
Angels guide the souls of the righteous, but demons will seize the souls of the wicked.
Wherever evil enters, there also is ignorance, but the hearts of the holy will be filled with knowledge.
A merciless monk will be in need, but the one who feeds the poor will inherit treasures.
Better is poverty with knowledge than wealth with ignorance.
A crown is the ornament of the head, but knowledge of God is the ornament of the heart.
Acquire knowledge and not silver, and wisdom rather than great wealth.
The righteous will inherit the Lord, and the holy will be nourished by him.
The one who has mercy on the poor destroys anger, and the one who feeds them will be filled with good things.
Wisdom will rest in a gentle heart, and an active soul is the throne of freedom from passions.
Craftsmen of evil will receive an evil wage, but craftsmen of good will be given a good wage.
The one who sets a trap will be caught in it, and the one who hides it will be captured by it.
Better is a gentle worldly man than a wrathful and irascible monk.
Anger scatters knowledge, but patience gathers it.
As a strong south wind on the open sea, so is anger in a man's heart.
The one who prays continually escapes temptations, but thoughts trouble the heart of the negligent one.
Do not let wine gladden you or meat delight you, lest you fatten the flesh of your body and shameful thoughts never leave you.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
The superscription is its own paragraph, before saying 1.
orientation: Evagrius opens his collection of sayings by addressing monks who live in communities, calling them heirs of God and urging them to receive and pass on divine words.
